summary: Presented as an illustrated classroom lesson led by three student presenters, this educational comic explores three iconic pieces of NASA hardware deployed across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. For each mission, the presentation breaks down what the equipment is, how its technology works, and the groundbreaking scientific discoveries it made possible:
details: This educational comic teaches readers about real-world space exploration by showcasing the history, science, and lasting legacy of retired space rovers and landers. Specifically, it highlights how these machines gathered data on the Moon and Mars and explains why their scientific discoveries remain valuable long after their missions have ended. Connects hardware to real science: Readers see how specific parts—cameras, wheels, scientific instruments, and antennas—actually work to capture images, study rocks and soil, measure atmosphere and dust, and send data back to Earth. Long-term value of discovery: The project aims to show that even when a machine stops working or completes its mission, its discoveries remain valuable and continue helping scientists understand worlds like Mars. Developed using ChatGPT for brainstorming and story structure, and Canva to design, layout, and finalize the comic pages.Emotional Framing of Technology: Rather than treating retired rovers as broken scrap, it frames them as heroic pioneers with lasting stories ("Old machines. Real discoveries. A brighter tomorrow.").Audience Accessibility & Age Appeal: Using friendly, stylized characters, short speech bubbles, and clear headlines makes complex aerospace concepts easy for younger readers and general audiences to grasp.
